lines.t: [hook]Only playing *aces*?
That costs you [cost]*ten* big blinds | every time you wait.
And when they finally come, | [nobody0]*nobody* pays.
Here's the *maths*.
[grid]Your plan sounds simple enough:
[qq]*queens*, | [kk]*kings*, | [aa]*aces*,
and [ak]*ace-king*.
Everything else | goes straight in the [dim]*muck*.
Trouble is, | that's only [n34]*34* hands | out of 1,326.
Under [pct]*three percent* | of what you're dealt.
[wait]So mostly, | you fold.
And fold.
And fold some more, | because a premium comes round | about once every [n39]*39* hands.
[blinds]And while you wait, | the blinds don't.
Every orbit, | another one and a half big blinds | out of your stack.
So by the time the [aces]aces finally show up,
you've already paid about [paid]*ten* blinds | just to see them.
Now, at last, | you [raise]*raise*.
But the table has been [watch]*watching* you,
and you've played two hands | all hour.
So what happens? | [s1]Fold. | [s2]Fold. | [s3]Fold.
Your aces [win]win | one and a half blinds,
after you [net]paid *ten* | to get there.
[fix]So tight isn't the problem. | *Predictable* is.
Think about the [btn]button instead, | last to act,
where a solid player opens | about [widen]*38 percent* of hands:
[sc]suited connectors, | [pp]small pairs, | [ax]weak aces.
And now, when you raise, | nobody knows what you [nobody]*have*.
[sheet]So save this:
the later your seat, | the *more* hands you play.
Premiums are your floor, | never your whole *plan*.
[outro]So, honestly: | how long is *your* wait?
Tell me in the comments,
and [cta]run any spot free | at llama poker dot com.
